title: Uber Automates Dependency Analysis Across Its Service Mesh
gist: Uber built RPC-middleware instrumentation in YARPC that correlates caller and callee failures to classify service dependencies as fail-close, fail-open or unknown, after finding distributed-tracing sampling too slow to capture rare failures.

insights.claim: Uber classifies dependencies as fail-close (failure consistently causes the caller to fail), fail-open (failure does not break the caller) or unknown (insufficient evidence), and applies this across call paths to see how failures propagate to an originating API.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A reusable model for blast-radius analysis in large service meshes.

insights.claim: Uber computes a failure correlation probability per caller dependency: values >=0.8 are fail-close, <=0.2 fail-open, intermediate values unknown, with retries handled separately so they are not treated as independent dependencies.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Concrete thresholds that others can replicate.
insights.locator: Uber calculates a failure correlation probability

insights.claim: More than 99.9% of Uber requests complete without errors; at a 0.01% sampling rate and 99.9% availability an erroneous request has a one-in-10-million chance of being sampled, so at 500 requests per second capturing one failure could take 5 hours, 33 minutes and 20 seconds.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Sampled tracing is structurally poor for rare failures at scale.

insights.claim: Uber chose middleware metrics over distributed-tracing pipelines (even OpenTelemetry tail sampling), trading request-level detail for broader coverage and avoiding the overhead of storing and evaluating individual traces.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Metrics-based failure attribution is a cheaper alternative to trace storage, relevant to observability cost.

insights.claim: Uber routes service-to-service requests through the Muttley on-host proxy, which lacks caller endpoint context, so the analysis was added to YARPC (its Go and Java RPC framework) via inbound and outbound middleware.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Shows where infrastructure teams embed reliability instrumentation.

insights.claim: Inbound middleware generates a request ID and records caller service and endpoint in an in-memory RequestTracker; the ID propagates via Go context so outbound middleware records downstream service, endpoint and result, and metrics are emitted on completion.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Reproducible design for dependency mapping without tracing.
insights.locator: Inbound middleware generates a request ID

insights.claim: Uber says the approach has cataloged dependencies for critical APIs and indexed most fail-close anomalies across its service mesh.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Claim of production coverage, though not quantified.
